A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated background, proofs and experimental results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein-generation experiments on single-motif, multi-motif and symmetry tasks in Section 4, plus hyperparameter and sequence-requirement analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D and additionally reports computational-cost findings in Section 4.5.

M1.justification: The proposed potentials, Genie priors and sampler families are retained. However, v2 Appendix C.2 writes exp(-L/eta_t) while defining eta_t as reciprocal variance, conflicting with v1 Appendix B.2 and the retained main-text scaling. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedural change or a mathematical transcription error.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SCOPe-trained Genie models, 24 single-motif problems, six multi-motif problems, cyclic and dihedral generation tasks, and evaluations without fixed motif sequences. The benchmark specifications match after table renumbering.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain BPF-fw/bw, FPS-SMC, MCGDiff and the same TDS potential variants. Reconstruction-based BPF was already represented by zero guidance in the hyperparameter search. Newly discussed SVDD and PDDS are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 adds efficiency assessment through forward/backward model-pass counts and estimated speedup. Scaffolding evaluation retains its success thresholds, fixed motif placements, 1,000 denoising steps, eight particles, sample budgets and hyperparameter-search protocol; no benchmark rerun is established.

E4.justification: v2 adds a computational-efficiency analysis comparing sampler costs and potential complexity, extending v1's brief implementation-optimisation discussion. The noise, guidance and chirality sweeps and sequence-requirement analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing standard-deviation error bars and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained. No new seed information, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: New findings include TDS runtimes up to three times those of MCGDiff and backward passes taking about twice as long as forward passes. These are newly reported costs, not improvements over v1. Benchmark outcomes remain unchanged, including ten single-motif problems solved by TDS-rmsd and one unique success in each of two expanded multi-motif experiments.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit target-transition and twisting formulations, weight-update derivations in Appendix A.2, and complexity statements in Table 2. The potential definitions and chirality proof are retained. Its rewritten TDS proposal in Equation 15 introduces a cumulative-alpha prefactor absent from v1 Algorithm 5 and inconsistent with the retained DDPM parameterisation.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims substantial benefits from measurement-tilted proposals and twisted targets, and the introduction adds sampler design choices and empirical costs to the stated contributions. The central claims about guidance potentials, zero-shot multi-motif feasibility and symmetric generation remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting BPF performance to high-dimensional guidance, particle degeneracy to final-sample duplication, and model evaluations to runtime. Appendix A.2 discusses limiting resampling and parallel sampler instances as possible remedies. Existing sequence-information and fixed-placement limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies model-call and runtime information but replaces the separate sampler algorithms with a general recipe and formulas. In particular, the detailed noiseless-MCGDiff procedure in v1 Algorithm 4 is explicitly omitted. Checkpoints, hardware, tuning settings and code-access information remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds foundational SMC references by Del Moral and colleagues, Pitt and Shephard, and Johansen and Doucet, plus discussion of SVDD and PDDS within its sampler framework. The protein-design positioning and principal novelty claims remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The background is substantially reorganised around SMC design choices. DDPM and protein-structure primers move to Appendix A.1, the sampler appendix is restructured, and the abstract and several results passages are rewritten. A computational-cost section and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables, replaces four sampler algorithm displays with a unified recipe, redraws the motif-task schematic, relocates the protein-backbone figure and extensively changes typography and figure placement. The multi-motif chart reorders 2B5I and 3NTN together with their data; this is not a score change.

improvement.justification: The unified SMC explanation and computational-cost analysis improve interpretability. However, v2 omits detailed noiseless-MCGDiff instructions and introduces inconsistencies in likelihood scaling (Appendix C.2) and the TDS proposal (Equation 15). With the core experimental evidence unchanged, the exposition gains and mathematical/reproducibility drawbacks do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
